clue.text: In theory a profit appearing in another form

indicators.note: letters shown in another form are rearranged, so the preceding word is shuffled

explanation.surface: An economist explains that a profit on paper can look different in practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in another form' rearranges APPEARING. A gain that exists only on the books, not yet cashed, is a profit in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A gain recorded on the books but not yet realised in cash exists only as an accounting idea.

clue.text: She will see to our wants if we &go out after beer

definitions.text: She will see to our wants

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

indicators.note: letters that go out of their order are rearranged, so 'if we' is shuffled

explanation.surface: A landlady who looks after us when we head out for a pint.
explanation.walkthrough: The ampersand before 'go' is a print blemish. An alewife was a woman who kept an alehouse and served its customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the woman running an alehouse served drinkers, attending to their needs.

clue.text: People who consider themselves most important

definitions.text: People who consider themselves most important

parts.words: People who consider themselves most important
parts.note: a plain description of self-centred people who rank their own interests first

explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred individuals rate their own interests above everyone else's.

clue.text: A type of dragoman?

indicators.note: with the question mark, 'of' signals that the answer is a version made out of the following word's letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about what sort of interpreter someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: A dragoman is an interpreter in the Middle East; its letters rearranged give a typeface, the 'type' of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Garamond is a well-known serif typeface named after a sixteenth-century French punch-cutter.

clue.text: An elevated and unusually true character

indicators.note: in a down entry a word raised up reads from bottom to top, so 'An' is turned round
something done unusually is out of its normal order, so 'true' is rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a noble and uncommonly honest personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns AN into NA in this down clue; 'unusually' rearranges TRUE into TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's essential disposition or temperament is their makeup.

clue.text: Contractor required at the power-station?

parts.note: reads like a building firm hired for a job, but means a device that makes steam contract into water

explanation.definitionFit: A power station's cooling apparatus turns spent steam back into liquid, shrinking its volume.

clue.text: Marsh bird that got its teeth into an aquatic one?

parts.note: bit means got its teeth into
a tern is a sea bird, an aquatic one

explanation.surface: A wading bird snaps at a fellow water bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'bird', so 'an aquatic one' is a water bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a heron-like wader known for its booming call in reed beds.

clue.text: Suitable game for a racing trainer to play with his apprentices?

definitions.text: Suitable game for a racing trainer to play with his apprentices?

parts.words: Suitable game for a racing trainer to play with his apprentices?
parts.note: a card game whose first part is a place where racehorses are bred, fitting for a horseman

explanation.definitionFit: This is a poker variant in which some cards are dealt face up, and its first word also names a horse-breeding establishment.

clue.text: Type of philosopher who might find employment at Aldermaston?

definitions.meaning: a follower of the ancient theory that everything is made of indivisible particles

definitions.text: who might find employment at Aldermaston?
definitions.meaning: Aldermaston is the English site of Britain's nuclear weapons research establishment, so a nuclear scientist might work there

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a believer in Democritus's particle theory and a nuclear physicist.

clue.text: Round trips that take longer

parts.note: not a there-and-back journey but routes that go round an obstacle and so add distance

explanation.definitionFit: Roundabout routes taken to avoid a blockage add time to a journey.

clue.text: What the letters shouldn't be — or the typist, if she's pretty!

definitions.meaning: correspondence ought to carry a date

definitions.text: or the typist, if she's pretty!
definitions.meaning: an attractive typist should not be without anyone taking her out

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lacking a written date and not having been asked out on a date.

clue.text: Certainly not the day when everything gets curiously dimmer outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit outside, around the word for everything
curiously signals that the letters of 'dimmer' are rearranged in an odd way

parts.note: sum means the total, everything

explanation.surface: A gloomy day when the light fades all round.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is ironic: the longest day of the year, with the most daylight, is the last day anyone would call dimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The year's longest day, at the summer solstice, has the most daylight and so is hardly gloomy.

clue.text: Went quietly by, inordinately pleased

indicators.note: inordinately means out of order, so the letters of 'pleased' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Time passed peacefully and someone was extremely happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inordinately' looks like 'excessively' but here it rearranges PLEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone past unnoticed has slipped away.

clue.text: Renaissance genius who painted a heavenly sign on a road intersection

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: at an intersection paths cross and mix, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An Italian master painted a star sign at a crossroads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a heavenly sign' is a zodiac sign; 'intersection' suggests paths crossing, so the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Vinci was the archetypal Renaissance polymath and the painter of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Why Engineers like getting on?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
as means like
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking why army engineers get along so well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why' is a noun here: 'the why' of something is its cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The cause or motive behind something is its explanation.

clue.text: Making a place as good as new or doing nothing about it?

definitions.text: Making a place as good as new

indicators.note: the word for doing nothing goes about, around, the word 'or'

parts.note: resting means doing nothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: Renovating a house, or idly leaving it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like it joins two definitions, but it is a letter piece placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Renovating a building brings it back to its original condition.

clue.text: Where village hops might be held in Kent

definitions.text: Where village hops might be held in Kent

parts.words: Where village hops might be held in Kent
parts.note: reads as a venue for country dances, but means a kiln building for drying the hop plant; Kent is a county in south-east England famous for hop growing

explanation.definitionFit: Kentish farms dry harvested hops in distinctive cowled kiln buildings.

clue.text: Far from thin girl turning to sit for her portrait?

indicators.note: turning means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ida is a girl's name
to pose is to sit for a portrait

explanation.surface: A plump young woman turns to model for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sit for her portrait' reads as the girl's purpose, but it supplies a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fatty, describing tissue storing fat, so someone stout.

clue.text: Allow a penalty, possibly

definitions.meaning: a punitive measure, such as trade restrictions on a country

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both official approval and a punitive measure, two nearly opposite senses.

clue.text: Stand for a lesson?

parts.note: not tolerating a class, but a reading desk for a Bible reading in church

explanation.definitionFit: A church reading desk holds the book for the scripture reading, called the lesson.

clue.text: Men trained to shoot back with grim enthusiasm

indicators.note: back means the gunners' abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, gunners of the British Army
dour means grim

explanation.surface: Gunners return fire with stern zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men trained to shoot' are gunners, the Royal Artillery, a standard crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour or passion is intense eagerness.

clue.text: They are simply regarded as songs

definitions.text: They are simply regarded as songs

parts.words: They are simply regarded as songs
parts.note: describes short, simple tunes thought of as nothing more than light verses

explanation.definitionFit: Short simple songs are light verses set to tunes.

clue.text: Stray noun we'd reclassified

indicators.note: reclassified means sorted again in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which a noun is assigned to a different category.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray animal has no keeper or owner.

clue.text: It deals with something formally in writing

definitions.text: It deals with something formally in writing

parts.words: It deals with something formally in writing
parts.note: describes a systematic written discussion of a subject

explanation.definitionFit: A formal written work examines a subject systematically.

clue.text: Was brought up to have a look at a piece of playground equipment

parts.note: to see is to have a look at

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means read from the bottom upward, turning 'was' round

explanation.surface: Someone raised to go and inspect a swing or slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like 'raised as a child', but in a down entry it reads a word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A teeter-totter is a plank balanced on a pivot for children to ride.

clue.text: Cautioned anew, the truant has scant regard for it

definitions.text: the truant has scant regard for it

indicators.note: anew means made again in a fresh form, so the letters of 'Cautioned' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A truanting pupil, warned again, still ignores school.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is what a pupil who skips classes neglects.

clue.text: Crumpled hat in part sprayed with pesticide, maybe

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go in the word for part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: crumpled means crushed out of shape, so the letters of 'hat' are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's crushed hat in a scene is doused with bug spray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crumpled' rearranges HAT to ATH, put 'in' ROLE. The definition describes a rodent's burrow as a place that might be treated with poison.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodent's burrow is a spot that pest control might treat.

clue.text: Dreams we get six to one on amidships

annotationWithheld.why: Dreams we get six to one on amidships: VI + I + ON inside SS needs 'amidships' to supply SS (ship) and the containment at once, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Dreams we get six to one on amidships

clue.text: Newly risen Salvation Army girl becomes Portia's maid

indicators.note: newly means made in a new form, so the letters of 'risen' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl in the Salvation Army gets promoted to a lady's maid.
explanation.walkthrough: Portia is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, whose waiting-woman bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice, the heroine's waiting-woman and confidante bears this name.

clue.text: Unfavourable aspect of battered snow ridge?

indicators.note: battered means knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A snowdrift hit by the wind shows its worst face.
explanation.definitionFit: The disadvantageous or harmful face of something is its bad flank.
